basic_information.official_title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE USE OF FIFTY MILLION PESOS (PHP 50,000,000.00) FOR THE ACQUISITION OF ADDITIONAL OXYGEN TANKS TO BE CHARGED AGAINST THE 2021 QUICK RESPONSE FUND ON HEALTH OF THE BANGSAMORO GOVERNMENT
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Releases ₱50 million from the region's health emergency fund to buy oxygen tanks for hospitals and health facilities across the BARMM, to be shared out equitably among the provinces.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: It was passed in August 2021, during the pandemic's most severe wave, when medical oxygen was the binding constraint on treating critically ill patients. The act is an emergency purchase — a buffer stock, as its own short title says.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The Ministry of Health received ₱50 million specifically for additional oxygen tanks, distributed equitably across the provinces, and was required to publish the details of that distribution on its transparency seal.
who_will_be_affected: Patients needing medical oxygen in any health facility in the region
Hospitals and health facilities across all provinces of the BARMM
The Ministry of Health, which receives and spends the money
Taxpayers, since the ₱50 million came from the 2021 Quick Response Fund on Health
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication in 2021. The purchase it authorised is complete or lapsed; the act remains on the books.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: SPENT. ₱50 million of emergency health money was released in 2021 to buy oxygen tanks for hospitals across the region, shared out among the provinces — and the Ministry of Health was required to publish where it went.
in_practice: ₱50,000,000 charged against the 2021 Quick Response Fund on Health
Spent specifically on additional oxygen tanks — the act names no other use
Distributed equitably among the different provinces of the BARMM
Released by the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management to the Ministry of Health
The Ministry of Health must post the details of distribution on its transparency seal

for_specific_groups.Patients: The point of the act is that a health facility in your province has oxygen when you need it.
for_specific_groups.Provincial health facilities: Distribution is required to be equitable across provinces, not concentrated where the biggest hospitals are.
for_specific_groups.Anyone checking where the money went: Section 5 requires the Ministry of Health to publish the distribution details on its transparency seal — this is a rare, express publication duty.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: The purchase was made in 2021; the tanks remain in the health system.
what_you_can_do: Look for the fund distribution details on the Ministry of Health's transparency seal — the act requires them to be posted
watch_out_for: 'Equitably distributed' is not defined — no formula, no per-province allocation, and no requirement to publish one.
The act sets no deadline for the purchase and no reporting date.
No penalty attaches if the transparency duty in Section 5 is not met.

key_terms_explained.Quick Response Fund: A standing pot of money government keeps for emergencies so it does not have to pass a new budget in a crisis.
key_terms_explained.Transparency seal: A page a Philippine government agency is required to maintain publishing its budget, projects and spending.
key_terms_explained.Buffer stock: A reserve held so supply does not run out under a sudden surge in demand.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Muharram 15, 1443 / 24 August 2021, approved by the Chief Minister on 22 September 2021.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Health (MOH), which holds and spends the fund
where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM), which releases it, under the usual accounting and auditing rules
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A district hospital in Tawi-Tawi runs short of medical oxygen during a surge. This act funded additional tanks distributed across the provinces so supply did not depend on reaching Cotabato City.
A resident wants to know how the ₱50 million was split between provinces. Section 5 requires the Ministry of Health to include the distribution details in what it posts on its transparency seal.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Oxygen Buffer Stock of 2021”.
Section 2 — Authorises ₱50,000,000 from the 2021 Quick Response Fund on Health for the acquisition of additional oxygen tanks in the BARMM.
Section 3 — The additional oxygen tanks are to be equitably distributed among the different provinces of the BARMM to ensure a sufficient supply of medical oxygen in the Region's health facilities.
Section 4 — The fund is released by the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management to the Ministry of Health, subject to the usual accounting and auditing laws, rules and regulations.
Section 5 — The Ministry of Health shall ensure the details of fund distribution are included in the information posted on its transparency seal.
Section 7 — Takes effect immediately after publication.

citizen_questions.q: How much was spent, and on what?
citizen_questions.a: ₱50 million, on additional oxygen tanks — the act authorises nothing else.

citizen_questions.q: Where did the money come from?
citizen_questions.a: The 2021 Quick Response Fund on Health of the Bangsamoro Government, the standing pot kept for emergencies. It was not a new appropriation.
Health facilities across the region. Section 3 requires equitable distribution among the different provinces of the BARMM, though it does not define what equitable means.

citizen_questions.q: Can I find out how it was divided up?
citizen_questions.a: Section 5 requires the Ministry of Health to include the fund distribution details in what it posts on its transparency seal.
No. It authorised a single purchase in 2021.
